title: Care and Keeping of Components: contribution, review, RFC & deprecation runway
creator: Sofia Martínez
description:
Goal: create a single, pragmatic maintenance guide for design contributors that covers token hygiene, component changes (buttons, tables, charts), RFC triggers, review checklist, and an operator-friendly deprecation runway. This ticket captures the canonical contribution flow, automated checks, and a lightweight governance model so designers and engineers can make safe, measurable updates without delaying product teams.

Scope: tokens (naming, aliases, breaking changes), component API/props changes, visual spec updates, documentation/Storybook, accessibility gating, performance/renderer considerations for charts and large tables, and a standard deprecation timeline for consumers. This guide is intentionally implementation-agnostic but includes examples for React/Storybook and the Redwood Console.

Principles: clear ownership, small/composable changes, backwards-compatible aliases where possible, measurable migration signals, and automated enforcement to reduce review friction.
acceptance_criteria: A1: Contribution steps documented (new token, token rename, component prop change, visual refresh) with required checklist items for each path.
A2: A concise RFC trigger table that maps change types to required review bodies and minimum notice windows.
A3: Review checklist exists and is included as a PR template; checklist covers accessibility, visuals, tokens, tests, Storybook, changelog, and consumer migration note.
A4: Deprecation runway is documented with timeline examples (soft deprecate, warnings, removal) and automation ideas for runtime warnings and static analysis.
A5: Links to example RFCs, migration guides, and a sample GitHub PR that follows the checklist are embedded in the doc.
A6: Design + Eng sign-off flow defined and owners assigned for token families and charts/tables components.
notes: 2025-02-12: Kickoff meeting with Design, Eng platform, and Docs. Agreed on single-source doc in Confluence and PR checklist in repo.
